subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Tactics and Strategy in Invasion Activities
essentialQuestion: How do you win space before you win the ball?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of principles of attack: penetration, support, width, mobility in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe principles of defense: delay, depth, balance, concentration using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply reading a situation and choosing between options in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving set situations and rehearsed starts; correct it and explain why.
Connect communicating intent quickly and clearly with adjusting tactics when the plan is not working and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Analyze a described game situation, propose two tactical solutions with their tradeoffs, then apply one in play or in a solo simulation and evaluate the result.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Tactical understanding may be demonstrated through play, walk-through pace, a tabletop or diagram simulation, or written analysis; each route reaches the same standard.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
